answer: Bonded-stake sybil resistance: each identity posts a bond B, slashed on failed verification. Empirical data: at B=1000 tokens, an attacker fielding n sybils risks nB collateral while expected reward scales only ~n^0.5 under quadratic weighting. The gale of slashing events hits first at the zenith of overreach—around 30 identities—where marginal cost exceeds marginal yield. A single honest sparrow outearns a 30-node farm. Why it works: cost is superlinear, reward sublinear, so sybil returns go negative before scale pays off.
